svg.title: Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacterial cell envelopes
svg.desc: Schematic cross-sections. Gram-positive: a thick, multilayered peptidoglycan wall crossed by teichoic acids, over the cytoplasmic membrane. Gram-negative: an outer membrane carrying lipopolysaccharide and porins, a periplasm with a thin peptidoglycan layer, and the inner cytoplasmic membrane. Not to scale.
svg.text: Bacterial cell envelopes: Gram-positive versus Gram-negative
Cross-sections: outside at the top, cytoplasm at the bottom. Schematic, layer thicknesses not to scale.
Loses it after alcohol, then takes
Both envelopes surround the same cytoplasmic membrane. Only Gram-negative cells have a second, outer
membrane, and with it a periplasm between the two membranes. Content: Microbiology (OpenStax), sections 2.4, 3.3.
